cards.statement: Amazon SNS filters a subscription using payload fields when the developer sets FilterPolicyScope=MessageBody.
cards.explanation: FilterPolicyScope=MessageBody directs SNS to evaluate the subscription filter against payload properties. Put the relevant filtering fields in the message body.

source.title: Amazon SNS subscription filter policy scope

cards.statement: Amazon SNS uses OR across property names in a subscription filter policy that omits the $or operator.
cards.explanation: SNS combines conditions on different filter-policy properties with AND unless an explicit $or relationship applies. A matching message satisfies the property conditions together.
cards.misconception: Conditions on different SNS filter-policy properties are alternatives rather than combined requirements.

cards.statement: With gzip caching enabled, Amazon CloudFront reduces Accept-Encoding: gzip,deflate to gzip in cache keys by default.
cards.explanation: CloudFront includes the normalized compression header in the cache key. For a gzip-enabled cache policy, extra encodings such as deflate do not create separate cache entries.

cards.statement: A browser can keep serving a cached file after Amazon CloudFront finishes invalidating that file.
cards.explanation: CloudFront invalidation removes the file from its edge caches. A copy in a browser's cache can remain usable until that cache entry expires.

cards.statement: Amazon API Gateway enables POST caching by default when a developer turns on REST API stage-level caching.
cards.explanation: The REST API stage's default method cache setting applies to GET methods. Enable a method override explicitly to cache POST responses.
cards.misconception: Enabling the REST API stage's default method cache also enables caching for POST methods.
cards.volatilityNote: AWS could revise which REST API methods receive caching through the stage's default setting.

source.title: Cache settings for REST APIs in API Gateway

cards.statement: Amazon DynamoDB UpdateItem applies numeric ADD updates atomically under concurrent writes.
cards.explanation: Use an ADD update expression to increment the stored counter value inside DynamoDB. Concurrent increments avoid a client-side read-modify-write race.

source.title: Use atomic counter operations in DynamoDB with an AWS SDK

cards.statement: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) supports cache hits for GetItem requests with ConsistentRead=true.
cards.explanation: DAX forwards a GetItem request with ConsistentRead=true to DynamoDB. It returns the response to the client but does not cache that result.
cards.misconception: DAX serves strongly consistent GetItem reads from its item cache.

cards.statement: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS can enforce atomic execution for a command batch through pipelining alone.
cards.explanation: Pipelining reduces waiting for network responses. MULTI and EXEC provide atomic transaction execution; ordinary pipelining does not add that guarantee.
cards.misconception: Sending Redis OSS commands as a pipeline makes the batch execute as an atomic transaction.

source.title: Optimize Redis Client Performance for Amazon ElastiCache and MemoryDB

cards.statement: Amazon SQS uses a weighted subset of queue servers for ReceiveMessage requests that use long polling.
cards.explanation: With long polling, ReceiveMessage queries the full set of SQS servers for the queue. Broader server coverage reduces false empty responses.
cards.misconception: Long polling waits longer while querying the same sampled subset of servers as short polling.

source.title: Amazon SQS short and long polling

cards.statement: Amazon ECS supports CPU use above a container's cpu reservation for Linux containers hosted on Amazon EC2.
cards.explanation: For Linux containers on EC2, the container-level cpu setting supplies relative CPU shares. Spare host CPU can be used above that reservation, subject to task-level limits.

cards.statement: For MySQL, Amazon RDS Proxy pins the session when a client executes CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE.
cards.explanation: The temporary table's state belongs to that database session. RDS Proxy preserves it by keeping subsequent transactions on the same underlying connection.

cards.statement: In a reused Python Lambda environment, the REPORT line's Max Memory Used measures the current invocation's peak.
cards.explanation: For invocations sharing a Python Lambda execution environment, Max Memory Used reports the highest memory use across those invocations. An earlier peak can affect a later REPORT line.
cards.misconception: REPORT's Max Memory Used is an invocation-specific peak that resets when Lambda reuses an execution environment.
cards.volatilityNote: Lambda could refine REPORT memory statistics to report an invocation-specific peak.

source.title: Log and monitor Python Lambda functions
